thread.title: Diez: NASCAR's playoff chase comes down to final race
thread.title_full: Diez: NASCAR's playoff chase comes down to final race

author: Roger Diez
title: Diez: NASCAR's playoff chase comes down to final race
text:
Last Saturday night at Richmond Raceway, Austin Dillon won the Cook Out 400, making amends for last year. This time he won cleanly without punting drivers on the last lap like a bowling ball picking up a 7-10 split. He is the 14th driver to score a berth in the playoffs with only one regular-season race to go. William Byron clinched the regular-season championship at Richmond when Chase Elliott was taken out in a pileup on lap 198 and finished 38th.
•••
The Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona is this weekend on NASCAR’s second-longest track, a high-banked, 2.5-mile oval. It is the last chance for a driver to lock into the playoffs with a win. And Daytona is a track where unlikely winners prevail more often than not. Harrison Burton scored his only Cup victory a year ago, and Justin Haley did so in 2019. One of Erik Jones’ three career wins came at the Coke Zero 400, as did one of Ricky Stenhouse Jr.’s four. Both Chris Buescher and Dillon have one of their six career wins at this race. Coke Zero 400 winners who are more familiar with Victory Lane include Ryan Blaney (2021) and Brad Keselowski (2016). Byron won in 2020 and the Daytona 500 this year, while Denny Hamlin has three Daytona 500 wins but is winless in the 400.
•••
If we have a new winner Sunday, there will be 15 of the 16 playoff berths locked in and Tyler Reddick will be the only driver to qualify on points. If there is a repeat winner, both Reddick and Alex Bowman are in the playoffs. If either one of those two wins tomorrow, the other will make it on points. The next three, Ryan Preece, Buescher, and Kyle Busch are in a must-win situation if they are to land a playoff spot. Saturday’s schedule calls for Xfinity practice and qualifying at noon and the Wawa 250 at 4:30 p.m., both on the CW. NASCAR Cup practice and qualifying airs at 3 p m. on Tru, with Sunday’s Coke Zero 400 broadcast on NBC and Peacock.
•••
The NTT IndyCar series is back in action this weekend at the hallowed Milwaukee Mile, the second longest-running venue for the series after the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. The first Milwaukee race was held in 1937 and was sanctioned by AAA until 1955. USAC took over from 1956-1979, CART/Champ Car from 1980-2007, and IndyCar, 1996 to present. Only four active drivers have scored wins at the short, flat oval. Scott Mclaughlin and Pato O’Ward split last season’s doubleheader, Will Power won in 2018 and Scott Dixon in 2009. The last two races of the season, Milwaukee and Nashville, are somewhat anticlimactic given that Alex Palou wrapped up the championship two weeks ago in Portland. O’Ward’s second place in the point standings is secure but both Christian Lundgaard and Kyle Kirkwood are within striking distance of Dixon in third place. And there is a real fight for sixth place among four drivers, all within an 11-point spread. In order they are Will Power, Felix Rosenqvist, Colton Herta, and Marcus Armstrong. Saturday, Practice 1 and qualifying air on FS1 at 8 and 9 a.m. , espectively. FS2 will broadcast final practice at 1:30 p.m. Sunday’s race is on Fox at 11 a.m.
•••
In other news, NASCAR’s Xfinity series will have a new name next season, with O’Reilly Auto Parts as the series sponsor. Also, Portland winner Will Power still does not have a contract with Team Penske for 2026. If he doesn’t get one, Rahal Letterman Lanigan has expressed an interest in signing him and Meyer Shank Racing and A.J. Foyt Racing are also possibilities. We’ll know after Nashville.
